title: Year four opens: how it all works
hook: three years of story, text and history; now the machinery: law, thought, streams, character, language

segments.voice: Yesterday, year three closed with stones on the far bank of the Jordan, and your line: the story goes on. Today, a new year begins.

A watch lies face down on a repair bench. For years its owner only saw the front: two hands going round, the hours passing. Then the jeweler pries off the back. Tiny wheels with teeth. A spring wound tight. Something rocking back and forth, steady as breath. The watch tells the same hours it always told, but now you can see why it keeps going. Three years on this path were the front of the watch: stories, the text, a people's history. This year, the back comes off.
screen: `A WATCH, FACE DOWN.` → `THE BACK COMES OFF.` → `SAME HOURS, NOW YOU SEE WHY.`

segments.voice: Year four opens. The first three years asked what happened, and what the text says. This year asks how it works. How does a verse become a practice on a Tuesday night? Who decides, and how do they argue? Here's the machinery, in the order the year opens it. First, law: the Mishnah and the Talmud, read plainly. The oral teaching, how it's arranged, how a page of argument turns into a way of living. Second, thought: Maimonides, who tried to show reason and faith working together, then the mystics of Kabbalah and the Hasidic teachers, who looked for hidden light. Third, the streams: the movements of Jewish life today, each described in its own terms, with no ranking. Fourth, character: Mussar, the old discipline of working on your traits one at a time, speech, anger, patience. Fifth, the life cycle and the language: birth to mourning, then the Hebrew letters and roots under every word you've met. A line in the Psalms fits a year like this. In the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "Open Thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Thy law." It doesn't ask for new law, or a different text. The same Torah, with eyes opened to what was already in it. Nothing you've learned is set aside. The stories and the history stay; this year shows the gears that kept them turning.
screen: `WHAT HAPPENED, THEN HOW IT WORKS.` · `LAW: THE MISHNAH AND THE TALMUD.` · `THOUGHT, STREAMS, CHARACTER.` · `THE LIFE CYCLE AND THE LANGUAGE.` · then, large: `OPEN THOU MINE EYES.`

segments.voice: Let one question rise that you'd like answered this year: why a custom is done the way it is, how a rule got decided, what a Hebrew word really holds. Skip the clever one and keep the one you actually want to know. If you pray, the psalm's words, open Thou mine eyes, are there to borrow.
Year four opens. Three years of story, text and history, and now the machinery behind them: law, thought, streams, character, language. Today's word.
Your line: now, how it works. Every question you bring is welcome here. Year four has begun.

chat.meaning: Year four sets nothing aside; it opens the machinery behind the stories: law, thought, streams, character, the life cycle and language.

Mishnah.meaning: the first written collection of the oral teaching

Talmud.meaning: the Mishnah together with the rabbis' long discussion of it

Maimonides.meaning: a medieval Jewish thinker who joined reason and faith

Kabbalah.meaning: Jewish mystical teaching that looks for hidden light

Mussar.meaning: the discipline of working on your character traits
